_comment: #253: the web save port END TO END in a real browser -- Export Save (blob download captured by the runner) then Import Save (a browser file chooser the runner answers with that download), both rows tapped by REAL touch so the file input opens inside a user gesture. Natively the taps are emulated and the headless arms run (export file + newest-export import), so the script doubles as a native regression of save_port_loop's row geometry. Web: run_web_qa.sh save_port_web 9 --skip-export --touch --device=iphone.

steps._comment: == EXPORT == pause -> Settings (row index 7) -> down x14 to 'Export Save' (index 14). GH#386 (v0.19 L5) regrouped the settings ROWS gameplay-first, so the save-file pair sits two rows further down than the append-order it landed in; nothing else in this script moved.
steps.name: cancel

steps._comment: #253 WEB ARM. Rows are 1-based like click_settings_row: 15 = Export Save, 16 = Import Save... (the keyboard idiom in save_port_loop moves down 14 then 1). Export on the web is a blob download the runner captures; the tap is a REAL browser touch so the import's file input opens inside a user gesture -- the exact condition mobile Safari/Chrome enforce and the engine-injected keyboard confirm cannot satisfy.

IMPORT: the tap must open a browser file chooser (the runner answers it with the export it just captured). game_loaded{reason:import} + save_imported prove the round trip landed; the refusal toast must NOT appear.
arm is web on the runner, headless natively -- the ROUND TRIP is the pin, not the arm
